assertion: DHS is reducing your rent / states and cities with the most ICE cooperation and deportations are seeing the largest rent decreases because removing 'illegals' cuts housing demand
warehouse_value: AskAmerica's own econ.regional_price_parities (BEA) shows Austin's rent-price index already declining from its 2023 peak (126.36) to 2024 (120.36), and Houston declining from 2022 (107.8) to 2024 (104.5) -- a downturn already underway a full year or more before the 2025-26 ICE enforcement surge this article credits
sql: SELECT geo_name, "year", rpp_index FROM econ.regional_price_parities WHERE tablename='MARPP' AND line_code='3' AND (geo_name ILIKE '%Austin%' OR geo_name ILIKE '%San Antonio%' OR geo_name ILIKE '%Dallas%' OR geo_name ILIKE '%Houston%') AND "year" >= 2019 ORDER BY geo_name, "year"
independent_value: Realtor.com data shows 37 consecutive months of YoY rent declines in the nation's 50 largest markets as of August 2026 -- a streak that began in 2023, under the prior administration, well before the current mass-deportation escalation -- driven by a documented multifamily construction oversupply (Austin alone added ~120,000 units, a 30% stock increase, 2015-2024). Meanwhile non-cooperating, high-immigration metros New York City and San Francisco saw rents RISE in 2026 (~+1.5% and +11.9% respectively) -- the opposite of what the 'fewer immigrant competitors' mechanism predicts if it were the dominant driver.
